claim.pdf_says: (13) For a file accessed in either random or dynamic access mode, the mass storage control system (MSCS)
claim.markdown_says: (13) For a file accessed in |║either║| random |║or dynamic║| access mode, the mass storage control system (MSCS)
claim.why_it_matters: The level-2 boxes around 'either' and 'or dynamic' are rendered with stray pipe characters outside the level marks (|║...║|), a notation used nowhere else in the transcription; the characters are not printed text and could be read as choice-indicator or alternation syntax.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 462 (VIII-32, Relative I-O REWRITE GR13) shows two single-line level-2 boxes, one around 'either' and one around 'or dynamic', and no vertical-bar glyphs outside them. The transcription (page-462.md line 5; specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 18166) writes '|║either║|' and '|║or dynamic║|'. The transcription's stated convention (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md lines 72-76) is that a box around words inside a sentence is written as '║words║', as in 'opened in the output ║or extend║ mode'. A grep finds the '|║'/'║|' form on only one line of the 1,853 lines that use ║, and that line is this one. So the two pairs of '|' characters are stray: they are not printed text and they break the box notation. The words themselves are correct and the level-2 boxing is kept, so the meaning does not change. Severity is cosmetic, as claimed. The fix is to write '║either║ random ║or dynamic║'.
